chunks: Whoever desires the fruits of the Hereafter, We shall add to his fruit. As for him who desires the fruits of this world, We shall give to him of these, but he will have no share in the Hereafter.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between seeking worldly gain and seeking the Hereafter according to Surah Ash-Shura?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of *Jihad al-Akbar* (striving for the Hereafter), where divine increase (*nazid*) signifies not just reward but the expansion of spiritual capacity and proximity to the Divine. It underscores the Shia emphasis on intention (*niyyah*) as the determinant of whether worldly efforts become mere sustenance or transformative acts of worship. The contrast highlights that worldly gain for the Hereafter-seeker is a bonus, whereas for the worldly-focused, it is their entire due, leaving them devoid of eternal merit.
